title: Review 1
description: Pronouns, noun gender, and the nominative case
descriptionRussian: Местоимения, род существительных и именительный падеж
intro: This review covers the foundations of Russian grammar: personal pronouns, noun gender, the nominative case, and basic question words. If you can use the right pronoun, determine a noun's gender, identify subjects in the nominative case, and form simple questions, you are ready to move forward.
rules: Personal pronouns: я (I), ты (you), он/она/оно (he/she/it), мы (we), вы (you formal/plural), они (they).
Noun gender is determined by the ending: consonant = masculine, -а/-я = feminine, -о/-е = neuter.
The nominative case is the default form used for the subject of a sentence: Мама читает (Mom reads).
In 'Это + noun' sentences, the noun is always in the nominative case: Это студент (This is a student).
Question words: кто (who), что (what), где (where), когда (when), почему (why), как (how).
examples: Я студент. Ты врач. Она учительница. (I'm a student. You're a doctor. She's a teacher.)
стол (m), книга (f), окно (n) — endings tell you the gender
Мама читает книгу. — Мама is the subject (nominative case).
Кто это? — Это Анна. (Who is this? — This is Anna.)

items.prompt: In the sentence 'Мама читает', which word is in the nominative case?
items.promptEnglish: In the sentence 'Мама читает' (Mom reads), which word is in the nominative case?
items.hint: The nominative case marks the subject
items.explanation: Мама is the subject (the one performing the action), so it is in the nominative case.

items.prompt: What is the correct pronoun for 'we' in Russian?
items.promptEnglish: What is the correct pronoun for 'we' in Russian?
items.explanation: Мы means 'we'. Вы is 'you (formal/plural)', они is 'they', ты is 'you (informal)'.
Nouns ending in -а or -я are typically feminine. Книга ends in -а, so it is feminine.
Nouns ending in -о or -е are neuter. Окно ends in -о, so it is neuter.

items.promptEnglish: Who is this? This is my brother.
items.explanation: Кто (who) is used when asking about people. Что (what) is for things.

items.prompt: Which word is the subject in 'Студент читает книгу'?
items.promptEnglish: Which word is the subject in 'The student reads a book'?
items.explanation: Студент is performing the action (reading), so it is the subject in the nominative case.
Они means 'they'. It is used for any group of people or things regardless of gender.

items.prompt: What is the nominative case used for?
items.promptEnglish: What is the nominative case used for?
items.explanation: The nominative case is the dictionary form and marks the subject, the person or thing performing the action.
